note: A curated atlas of the landmark Marvel comics — foundational first appearances and the major storylines the films and series adapt. Not every issue ever printed (that is tens of thousands); this is the source-material spine, broad across eras and verifiable. Dates are commonly cited cover/on-sale dates.
rows: The first Marvel (then Timely) comic — debut of the original Human Torch and the Sub-Mariner. The company's genesis.
First Captain America — the cover shows him socking Hitler a year before the U.S. entered the war.
Mr. Fantastic, Invisible Girl, Human Torch, The Thing
The comic that launched the Marvel Age — a bickering, human super-team. Ground zero of the shared universe.
First Hulk — Banner's gamma accident and his monstrous alter ego.
First Spider-Man — the radioactive spider bite and “with great power…” The best-selling key in comics.
First Thor of the Marvel Universe — Donald Blake finds Mjolnir in a Norwegian cave.
First Iron Man — Stark builds the grey armor to escape captivity. Vietnam in the comic, Afghanistan on screen.
First appearance of Ant-Man in costume, following Pym's debut in #27.
First Doctor Strange — Ditko's mind-bending Sorcerer Supreme.
Iron Man, Thor, Hulk, Ant-Man, Wasp
“And there came a day unlike any other…” The team assembles against Loki.
Cyclops, Marvel Girl, Beast, Angel, Iceman, Professor X, Magneto
First X-Men and Magneto — mutants feared by the world they protect.
Cap is found frozen in ice and revived into the modern age — the template for his MCU arc.
First Scarlet Witch and Quicksilver, as Magneto's Brotherhood.
First Daredevil — blinded by radioactive waste, the Man Without Fear.
First Hawkeye, initially a costumed criminal.
First Elektra — Miller's assassin and Matt's doomed love.
The Galactus Trilogy — first Silver Surfer and world-eater Galactus.
First Black Panther — T'Challa, king of Wakanda, the first mainstream Black superhero.
First (modern) Vision — the synthezoid who joins the Avengers.
First Mar-Vell; Carol Danvers debuts here on her road to becoming Captain Marvel.
The Surfer's tragic solo origin — Norrin Radd's bargain with Galactus.
First Ghost Rider — stunt rider Johnny Blaze bonded to a demon.
First Blade — the half-vampire Daywalker vampire hunter.
“The Night Gwen Stacy Died” — the snap that ended the Silver Age of innocence.
First Punisher — Frank Castle, introduced as a Spider-Man antagonist.
First Thanos and Drax the Destroyer — Starlin's cosmic mythology begins.
First Wolverine — a cameo in #180, full debut fighting the Hulk in #181.
The all-new, all-different international team that saved the franchise.
First Moon Knight — Marc Spector, avatar of Khonshu.
Jean Grey, Dark Phoenix, Kitty Pryde, Emma Frost
The Dark Phoenix Saga — Jean's corruption and sacrifice, the genre's defining tragedy.
“Days of Future Past” — the dystopian time-travel two-parter, endlessly adapted.
The Japan-set limited series that made Logan a character, not just a berserker.
Beyonder, most of the Marvel roster
The first company-wide crossover event; Spidey's black suit debuts here.
“Born Again” — Kingpin dismantles Matt's life; the definitive Daredevil story.
The limited series that spun Frank Castle off into his own ongoing war.
First full Venom — the symbiote finds its host. McFarlane's landmark.
Ross's painted, ground-level look at what it means to live among gods.
The best-selling comic book of all time; Jim Lee's blue-and-gold era.
Thanos, Adam Warlock, Nebula, the Avengers
Thanos wields all six gems and erases half of everything — the spine of the Infinity Saga.
The cosmic sequel; doppelgängers and Warlock's dark half.
A modern-day reboot of Spidey's origin — the tone the MCU would later borrow.
First Jessica Jones — a noir P.I. and survivor, Marvel's mature-readers debut.
Nick Fury, Captain America, Iron Man, Thor
The widescreen, Samuel-L-Jackson-Fury Avengers that directly shaped the MCU.
Kids discover their parents are supervillains and run.
“Disassembled” — Wanda's breakdown tears the team apart; the road to House of M.
First Kate Bishop and the Wiccan/Hulkling generation.
Scarlet Witch, Magneto, the X-Men, the Avengers
“No more mutants.” Wanda rewrites reality — the definitive chaos-magic story.
Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
The post-Disassembled reboot that made the Avengers Marvel's flagship again.
The cosmic war that rebuilt Marvel's space corner — the seedbed of the movie Guardians.
Registration splits the heroes — friend against friend over security vs. freedom.
Exiled to a gladiator planet, the Hulk becomes a king. The heart of Ragnarok.
The assassination of Steve Rogers on the courthouse steps after Civil War.
Brubaker brings Bucky back as a brainwashed assassin — the basis for the film.
The Hulk returns from exile to make Earth's heroes pay.
A future where the villains won and an old Logan takes one last ride.
“Who do you trust?” Shape-shifting Skrulls have replaced heroes for years.
The modern lineup that the films lifted almost wholesale.
First Gorr — the god-killer across three eras of Thor.
First Miles Morales — the new Spider-Man after Peter's death.
“The days Hawkeye isn't being an Avenger.” The tone of the Disney+ series.
The Phoenix returns and the two teams go to war over Hope.
First Kamala Khan — a Pakistani-American teen from Jersey City becomes Ms. Marvel.
Loki as a redemption-seeking trickster spy — the mischief the show runs on.
Universes collide into Battleworld — the modern template for the Multiverse Saga's finale.
A synthezoid builds a family in the suburbs and it curdles — WandaVision's soul.
Coates reinvents Wakanda as a nation in political turmoil.
A fractured-identity, is-it-real masterwork the series draws on directly.
Horror-tinged Hulk: he dies by day and rises by night. A modern high point.
First Loki of the Marvel Universe — Thor's adoptive brother and eternal antagonist.
Sgt. Fury and his Howling Commandos
First Nick Fury — WWII soldier before he ran S.H.I.E.L.D.
First Black Widow — Natasha Romanoff, Soviet spy turned Avenger.
First Doctor Octopus — Spidey's greatest foe.
First Green Goblin — the Osborn menace behind the mask.
First appearance of S.H.I.E.L.D. and Hydra in the modern era.
First Adam Warlock, created in a cocoon as “Him.”
First Ultron — the murderous A.I. built by Hank Pym.
First Guardians of the Galaxy — the original 31st-century team.
Doctor Strange, Hulk, Namor, Silver Surfer
First Luke Cage — the unbreakable hero of Harlem.
First Shang-Chi — the Master of Kung Fu.
Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings
First Iron Fist — the living weapon of K'un-Lun.
First Richard Rider — the human rocket of the Nova Corps.
First Eternals — Kirby's space-gods and their makers.
First Jennifer Walters — Banner's cousin, gamma-charged by his blood.
First full Rocket Raccoon (as later reimagined for the cosmic books).
First Beta Ray Bill — the alien who proved worthy of Mjolnir.
Carol Danvers takes the Ms. Marvel identity — her road to Captain Marvel.
The black suit arrives in the main title — the alien costume that becomes Venom.
First Nebula — space pirate and self-styled granddaughter of Thanos.
“Kraven's Last Hunt” — the hunter buries Spider-Man and takes his place.
First Mister Sinister — the geneticist obsessed with the Summers bloodline.
First Gambit — the charming Cajun who charges cards with kinetic energy.
First adult Cable — the time-travelling soldier son of Cyclops.
First Deadpool — the Merc with a Mouth, born as a Cable foil.
The line-wide alternate timeline where Xavier died and Apocalypse rules.
The psychic entity born of Xavier and Magneto that nearly ended the heroes.
Cyclops, Emma Frost, Beast, Kitty Pryde
Whedon's blockbuster run — the sensibility he carried into the Avengers films.
Every Spider-hero across the multiverse united — the comic that named the concept.
The Watcher, Nick Fury, the Avengers
The Watcher is murdered and everyone's secrets spill out.
Malekith's dark alliance invades Midgard — Aaron's Thor epic pays off.
Knull, god of the symbiotes, brings darkness to Earth.
First Riri Williams — the MIT prodigy who builds her own Iron armor.
Captain Marvel, Kree, Skrulls, the Avengers
The original Kree/Skrull War — the cosmic conflict the films draw their aliens from.
